title: Re-Verification of Earlier Warranty Work on Returned PAP Therapy Equipment
content:
# Re-Verification of Earlier Warranty Work — Returned PAP Therapy Equipment

**Protocol.** A self-pay PAP Therapy Equipment unit that comes back to Summit Ridge on a completed return pickup request and already had warranty repairs on its record has that work verified again on its return inspection. The count is of the repair jobs in the device's service history whose cost was borne under the manufacturer warranty:

- **two or more** manufacturer-warranty repairs: the unit goes through the full diagnostic protocol, and the labor units counted for the unit are increased by the labor units booked on all of those warranty jobs plus **2 protocol units**;
- **exactly one**: the labor units booked on that warranty repair job, **never less than 1 unit**, are added to the labor units counted;
- **none**: the labor units are booked as counted.

The labor units of a warranty job are the 15-minute units recorded on that job in the service history.

## Input — judgement — output

| Warranty repair jobs on the record | Labor booked on them (hypothetical) | Units added on the return inspection |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | — | 0 |
| 1 | 3 | 3 |
| 1 | 0 | 1 (never less than 1) |
| 2 | 3 and 4 | 3 plus 4 plus 2 protocol units, or 9 |
| 3 | 2, 2 and 5 | 2 plus 2 plus 5 plus 2 protocol units, or 11 |

**Basis questions.** *Do repair jobs whose cost was borne otherwise than under the manufacturer warranty count?* No; only manufacturer-warranty repairs are counted and summed. *Does the 1-unit minimum apply with two or more jobs?* The minimum belongs to the one-job line; with two or more jobs the units of all the jobs are summed and the 2 protocol units are added.
